messages:
mae: Morning team — handoff for the 06:00-14:00 UTC shift. Quick summary: small canary rolling, one scheduled migration, and a couple of watch items. TL;DR: watch KV eviction, GPU pool dropping on eu-west, and the analytics migration at 08:30 UTC.

mae: Changes since last shift:
- Canary for release/3.2.1 started by deploy-bot at ~05:45 UTC, traffic ramping slowly.
- Autoscaler bumped extra nodes in us-east due to spike; stable now.
- Analytics DB migration (schema v12) scheduled 08:30 UTC — low risk but long locks on small tables.

oncall-bot: deploy-bot: Canary deploy started for release/3.2.1 (canary id=can-20260318-11). Monitor /deploys/canary-can-20260318-11.

mae: What to watch:
- KV cache evictions: saw ~12% evictions on prefs shard at 05:30 UTC. If it goes >20% for >5m, raise priority and scale cache.
- eu-west GPU pool: free GPUs dipped to 1/6 after a batch job, could impact embeddings. If latency > 250ms p50 for embeddings, failover to us-east.
- Migration locks: DB locks might cause background jobs to pile up; expect delayed analytics events (<10m).

mae: Action items:
- jordan: please watch canary metrics and be ready to roll back. Reaction threshold: error rate >1% for 5m or 5x spike in p95 latency.
- sam: keep an eye on the KV eviction metric and increase cache replicas if sustained.
- ravi: ping infra-team if eu-west GPUs remain low after 06:30 UTC.
- liz: notify analytics owners when migration starts and confirm SLAs for delayed events.

jordan: on it. I’ll set an alert annotation for canary and keep a pager channel open. :thumbsup:

sam: noted. I pushed a small tweak to cache-autoscale in #pr-432 — low-risk. Can you ping me if evictions cross 15% so I can pre-scale?

mae: yes, will ping at 15% first. If it hits 20% I'll escalate.

ravi: FYI — I saw a queued batch job in eu-west that was supposed to finish at 04:50 but ran long (logs below). Might be the cause of GPU usage.

ravi: ```
2026-03-18T04:47:13Z batch-worker-03 ERROR long-runner: task-id=abcd1234 duration=3h12m started-by=nightly-scan
2026-03-18T04:49:09Z batch-worker-03 INFO evicting temp files
```

liz: I'll DM analytics owners and confirm they can tolerate the ~10m delay. If they want zero-drop, we'll need to pause migration and do a rolling approach.

jordan: small Q — if we hit the rollback threshold, do we want an immediate full rollback or stepwise? I'm leaning stepwise: decrease canary weight to 0, then rollback.

mae: stepwise is preferred. Decrease weight to 0, wait 2m. If errors persist, rollback to previous. Documented in runbook.

sam: popped a quick alert in Grafana for eviction >15% with a 3m evaluation window. Link: https://grafana.internal/r/evictions (pinning it to the oncall dashboard).

mae: thanks. Also note: scheduled infra maintenance for logging ingestion on 23rd 00:00 UTC — not relevant to this shift but flagging for next week.

jordan: small heads-up: a flaky test in ci/aws-integration has been failing intermittently; not related to prod but might block hotfix PRs. I’ll coordinate with QA.

mae: ok. Final: if anything looks noisy, call a quick async huddle in #oncall-room and @here for immediate eyeballs. Otherwise — normal ops. :eyes:

sam: ack. I’ll be around 06:00-13:30 UTC.

jordan: I'm on until 14:30 UTC.

ravi: standby until 09:00 UTC then on call overlaps.

liz: monitoring notifications set, will watch migration start.

mae: thanks all — passing the baton.

oncall-bot: shiftbot: Handoff complete. Next oncall: jordan.
